newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Guangzhou to expand Peugeot plant.
newsitem.headline: China's Guangzhou to expand Peugeot plant.

text.p: China's southern city of Guangzhou plans to expand the Sino-French Guangzhou Peugeot Automobile Co joint venture with investment of 7.0-8.0 billion yuan in the next three years, a provincial official said on Wednesday.

Annual production of the expanded group is expected to reach 150,000 automobiles, including trucks, from the current 50,000-60,000 cars, an offical of the Machine Building Department of Guangdong province said in a telephone interview.

The total investment in the project would be 7.0-8.0 billion yuan. The Guangzhou city government would invest 800 million yuan each year from 1997-1999, and the rest would be raised through bank loans and foreign funds, he said.
The first part of the government investment would be used to renovate the plant building and equipment this year, he said.
The government has yet to choose a foreign partner to cooperate in the expansion, he said.
Peugeot owns a 30 percent stake in the Guanggzhou company, which stopped producing cars several months ago amid a market slump.
Peugeot Automobile has said it had not decided to quit the joint venture amid French media reports that the project was on the brink of failure.
South Korean automaker Hyundai Motor Co has applied to Chinese authorities for a 22 percent stake in the Sino-French Guangzhou venture, Chinese media said last week.
Newspaper Le Monde said Hyundai, Opel and Bayerische Motoren Werke AG were lined up to take Peugeot's place if the French carmaker abandoned the project.
The China Daily Business Weekly said Hyundai's application for a stake had heated up competition among rivals Honda Motor Co, Ford Motor Co and BMW who are all interested in a role.
